tre_001: You can recognise it as Trento's oldest monumental tree, planted in 1835. It stands in the Giardino Martino Martini, off Via Santa Croce.
tre_002: You can recognise it by its trunk, 5.70 metres round, an unusually large size for a native black poplar, and by how much it moves in the wind. It stands in the Giardino di Largo Pigarelli.
tre_003: You can recognise it by standing just outside the railings of the Piazza Dante garden, on the street itself. It stands on Via Vannetti, facing the station.
tre_004: You can recognise it by standing about ten metres from a group of yews on the garden's north side, fast growing beside their slow one. It stands in the Giardino di Piazza Dante.
tre_005: You can recognise it by its trunk, 3.93 metres round, tucked into a corner of the garden where it takes some finding. It stands in the Giardino di Maso Ginocchio, Via Giusti.
tre_006: You can recognise it by its long needles and drooping branch tips, a more mournful posture than a Lebanon or Atlas cedar. It stands in the Parco di Gocciadoro.
tre_008: You can recognise it by its odd, barrel-like shape, a trunk 4.10 metres round on a tree only 10 metres tall. It stands on the Salita ai Spiazzi in Cortesano.
tre_010: You can recognise it by its trunk, 3.59 metres round, unusually thick for a wild cherry, on forest land near old war fortifications. It stands at Passo del Cimirlo, Casare.
